C-GENERIC-REVIEW-SCOPE-1-A7E352BF.Summary: Remove exactly one publisher-specific runtime privilege from the generic review surface: the ledger-backed WriteEvidence scope audit (`auditWriteEvidenceOutsideScope` / `review.write-evidence-outside-scope`) silently exempts every `docs/plans/` path via `isDocsPlansPath`. After this change a comparable WriteEvidence path under `docs/plans/` raises the same error as any other undeclared content path, and a matching declared `File` or relevant `Glob` makes it pass. The separate working-tree scope audit (`auditScopeOutsideWriteScope` / `review.scope-outside-write-scope`), the CLI lifecycle exclusions, the exact canonical engine candidate-lock exception and its near-miss refusals, finding deduplication/union/severity, and the missing/empty-evidence statuses are all preserved. No configurable bypass or new API is added. The historical rationalization in `C-DECLARED-WRITES` is explicitly overturned: a directory spelling establishes no consumer ownership, and concurrent work is coordinated through actual declared scope and evidence boundaries rather than a tool-defined path prefix.
C-GENERIC-REVIEW-SCOPE-1-A7E352BF.Problem:
Neo-grace is a generic methodology and CLI for developing other projects; this repository's tests, development archive corpus, CI, and authority records are internal implementation concerns and must not dictate consumer behavior. `C-DECLARED-WRITES` introduced the ledger-backed scope audit and, in `AC-LEDGER-SCOPE-RULE`, gave every path with prefix `docs/plans/` a tool-defined exclusion. Its own `Assumption` conceded that "any edit under `docs/plans/` that appears in WriteEvidence will not raise this finding." The exclusion was accepted because this repository had concurrent authority edits under that prefix and the residual was said to be process plus git history.
That argument does not generalize to a consumer project. `docs/plans/` is an arbitrary directory name; nothing about the spelling establishes that the repository owner authored the write, that the path is out of the executor's control, or that a declared `ObservedWriteScope` may not cover it. A consumer whose own roadmap lives under a different prefix — or which relies on the audit to notice an undeclared write under its roadmap — gets no such privilege. Concurrent work is coordinated through actual declared scope and evidence boundaries: a path that must change is declared in the plan's `ObservedWriteScope`, and a finding states that a recorded path is outside scope without inferring who authored it. The current behavior is a publisher-specific bypass inside a generic audit; this bundle removes it and makes documentation paths ordinary declared scope.
Removing the exemption is a surgical deletion of one predicate definition and its single bypass call plus the associated comments. The rest of the audit — union across attempts, deduplication, archive-identity expansion for `.ngrace/` bundle artifacts, the lifecycle and candidate-lock exceptions, the report fields, and the absence statuses — is unchanged. This is the first small bundle from the design's authorized cleanup; the remaining groups (generic archive-traversal restoration, the nine XML parser comment exceptions, other historical test consumers, and skill/resource/template cleanup) are separate bundles with their own stages and are NonGoals here. Skill-composition measurement and packaging/version repair are not asserted as defects owed by this cleanup; assessment of those surfaces is not an implementation decision of this bundle.

Goals.Goal: A WriteEvidence content path under `docs/plans/` that is not covered by the plan's `ObservedWriteScope` raises `review.write-evidence-outside-scope` with severity `error`, exactly as the same path would under any other undeclared prefix. `isDocsPlansPath` and its single bypass call are removed from `auditWriteEvidenceOutsideScope`; the finding is produced by the ordinary coverage path, not by a replacement exemption.

A `docs/plans/` path covered by an exact declared `File` or a relevant declared `Glob` does not raise, so declaring consumer documentation at plan time is sufficient and ordinary. Ordinary documentation coverage is exact-file or glob only. The audit adds no new way to declare, suppress, or configure coverage.

Every preserved boundary is provable: the separate working-tree audit still reports changed `docs/plans/` paths under `review.scope-outside-write-scope`; the CLI lifecycle exclusion (`run.xml`, `run-ledger.xml`, `run/**` under a canonical `C-*` bundle) and the exact canonical engine candidate lock are still filtered, with every near-miss still raising; undeclared approved `spec.xml`/`plan.xml` and other non-lifecycle `.ngrace/` content still raise; the same-ID `.ngrace/changes/{active,archive}/<id>/...` identity expansion for the reviewed change's own bundle artifacts remains while an undeclared path naming another change's bundle still raises; and path deduplication, union across attempts, finding code/severity, report fields, and the missing/empty-evidence statuses are unchanged.

Correct the catalog explanation of `review.write-evidence-outside-scope` so it no longer claims authority ownership of `docs/plans/`; state the path-class exclusions that remain (CLI lifecycle, exact canonical candidate lock) and that non-lifecycle `.ngrace/` paths raise.

Replace the affected publisher-history test expectations with ordinary synthetic fixtures. The direct `C-ESCALATION-HONESTY`/`docs/plans` exemption coupling and the whole-archive WriteEvidence multiset ratchet are removed and replaced by synthetic projects that preserve their useful generic controls: undeclared docs refusal, exact-file and glob declared docs success, undeclared ordinary path refusal, undeclared non-lifecycle `.ngrace/` refusal, lifecycle and candidate-lock near-miss refusals, and `unable-to-determine` on empty evidence. Existing byte-immutability, lifecycle, candidate-lock, and unrelated controls are kept, not deleted to obtain green.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-UNDECLARED-DOCS-PATH-RAISES: A WriteEvidence content path under `docs/plans/` that is not covered by the plan's `ObservedWriteScope` raises `review.write-evidence-outside-scope` with severity `error`, exactly as the same path would under any other undeclared prefix. Synthetic fixtures in `src/review/core.test.ts` prove, without consulting the repository archive: (a) an undeclared `docs/plans/active/<X>/decisions.md` and an undeclared `docs/plans/active/<X>/review.md` each produce exactly one finding whose code is the catalog constant `WRITE_EVIDENCE_SCOPE_FINDING_CODE`, whose severity is `error`, and whose `file` is that path; (b) an undeclared ordinary path `src/secret.ts` raises identically; (c) the same undeclared path repeated across WriteEvidence appearances still yields exactly one finding (deduplication); and (d) the union of content paths recorded on separate ledger and loose attempt events is audited, so a `docs/plans/` path present on only one attempt still raises. The finding shape and the `writeEvidenceScopeAudit` report fields (`status`, `reason`, `changeId`, `pathCount`, `findingCount`) are unchanged. Failure conditions: `docs/plans/` still silent; a replacement allowlist or one-off file list instead of ordinary coverage; dedup lost; only the last attempt consulted; severity lowered; finding or report fields renamed.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DECLARED-DOCS-PASSES: A WriteEvidence path under `docs/plans/` that is covered by the plan's `ObservedWriteScope` does not raise, by the same coverage rules the audit already uses: an exact declared `File` or a relevant declared `Glob`. Active↔archive identity expansion applies only to the reviewed change's own `.ngrace/changes/{active,archive}/<id>/...` bundle artifacts and does not alias ordinary `docs/plans/` paths. Synthetic fixtures prove each declared form passes with zero `review.write-evidence-outside-scope` findings, and that the coverage is not widened to swallow a sibling undeclared path. Missing or empty comparable WriteEvidence still yields `writeEvidenceScopeAudit.status === "unable-to-determine"` with a non-empty reason, never a clean `ran`; a change with at least one comparable path yields `ran` and `findingCount` may be 0. Failure conditions: declared docs path raises; glob coverage ignored; archive-identity expansion misapplied to ordinary `docs/plans/` paths; empty evidence reported as clean `ran`; coverage widened to a broader prefix.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PRESERVED-BOUNDARIES: The change is surgical and no preserved boundary moves. (a) The separate working-tree audit `auditScopeOutsideWriteScope` still reports changed `docs/plans/` paths under `review.scope-outside-write-scope`, distinct from the ledger code. (b) The CLI lifecycle exclusion still filters only `run.xml`, `run-ledger.xml`, and `run/**` under a canonical `C-*` bundle, never `spec.xml` or `plan.xml`. (c) The exact canonical engine candidate lock `.ngrace/changes/active/.candidate-<C-ID>.lock` for a valid canonical id is still filtered, and every near miss still raises: archive location, extra nesting, another top-level directory, and a malformed id. (d) An undeclared approved `spec.xml`/`plan.xml` and any other undeclared non-lifecycle `.ngrace/` content still raise. (e) The active↔archive identity expansion for the reviewed change's own `.ngrace/changes/{active,archive}/<id>/...` bundle artifacts remains, and a WriteEvidence path naming another change's bundle still raises when undeclared. (f) No configurable bypass, allowlist, override flag, configuration key, or new public API is introduced; the finding code remains bound to `WRITE_EVIDENCE_SCOPE_FINDING_CODE`. Failure conditions: porcelain audit changed or merged; lifecycle widened to all of `.ngrace/`; candidate-lock near miss silently exempted; non-lifecycle `.ngrace/` write silenced; other-ID bundle path aliased to the reviewed id; a new exemption surface added.
